_comment: Executable N11h review candidate: signed U10.1T8 190afedd base, host-only 65cc3535 -> 65ac5089. No boot or JAR changes.

fixes._comment: N11hCheckOwners() runs on EVERY spawn in the host StockCreateConfiguredNamespaces (key-independent): N11hResidentHandle does dlopen_ns(sealed owner, <owner path>, RTLD_NOW|RTLD_LOCAL|RTLD_NOLOAD) for liboh_adapter_bridge.so then liboh_android_runtime.so. Success = owner resident, handle non-null, rc=0 (ENOENT if missing). Two lines per spawn; the helloworld control prints it. Hard smoke per blueprint ('actual resident-check marker').

dlns_inherit(app_namespace, sealed owner, owner_shared) runs on EVERY spawn (unconditional app-domain edge; a 2nd inherit on bridge_namespace fires when wants_bridge). owner=westlake.sealed.child is a fixed literal. Success rc=0. Hard smoke per blueprint ('domain-inherit marker').

probe._probe_comment: N11h GOAL and the real gate: count by LOAD BASE, not inode/path. U9/U10.1 show liboh_adapter_bridge.so=2 and liboh_android_runtime.so=2 (two load-bases each; N11f/N11g proved the child is clean so the 2nd copy is host-side). N11h target = 1 each. libart.so + libopenjdkjvm.so are already single. Smoke MUST FAIL if either owner is still 2 -- that is exactly the single-owner gate.

advisory_fixes._comment: CONDITIONAL — do NOT hard-fail the control smoke on this. It fires only when the host StockOpenNamespace receives an exact owner-path request (N11hOwnerPath matches liboh_adapter_bridge.so / liboh_android_runtime.so): action=resident (returns the resident handle) or action=reject (handle=NULL). The owners are installed via dlns_inherit in StockCreateConfiguredNamespaces, so a spawn may find them resident WITHOUT re-requesting an owner open through this callback -- whether the helloworld control reaches this branch is UNVERIFIED. cx-t0: on the first smoke run, check if helloworld emits it; if it does not, DEMOTE this to a per-target assertion (assert on a session-miss target that reaches the owner-open path) and remove it from the control gate. Regex covers both resident and reject.
